title: Oregon Pet Safe Plants
text:
Welcome to Oregon Pet Safe Plants
    Helping pet parents find pet-safe native plants in Oregon
  
  


OregonPetSafePlants cross-references the ASPCA’s list of non-toxic plants with Oregon native plants documented in OregonFlora.org. By using this website, you acknowledge that you assume all responsibility for verifying plant safety before introducing any plant to an environment shared with pets.

title: About
text:
Our Approach
We cross-reference the ASPCA’s list of non-toxic plants with the Oregon native plant database maintained by OregonFlora.org, and highlight the species that appear on both lists. That overlap gives pet owners a starting point for landscaping and gardening choices that are both native to Oregon and generally considered pet-friendly.

title: About
text:
A Note on Safety
This site is meant to be a helpful starting point for your own research, not a substitute for professional advice. Individual pets can react differently to the same plant, and plant identification can be tricky. Always double-check with a trusted source, such as your veterinarian or the ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center, before introducing a new plant into a space shared with your pets.

text:
{{common_names}}
Rush Lily (Hastingsia alba) sends up tall spikes of small white flowers. It favors wet meadows and seasonal seeps, mostly in southwest Oregon.

title: Erythronium oregonum
text:
{{common_names}}
Fawn Lily (Erythronium oregonum) is a shade-loving woodland perennial native to western Oregon. Its nodding, white, lily-like flowers appear in early spring across Willamette Valley forests and shaded slopes.
